idiom_name: typed use-prefixed hooks returning tuples or objects (generic state, reducers, context)
implementation_notes: TypeScript changes nothing mechanically - the unit is still a plain function composing React's built-in hooks - but the types become part of the contract: useState<T> and reducer state/action unions pin the state shape, context hooks are typed via createContext<T> with an explicit null guard when there is no sensible default, and the returned tuple or object is the unit's published interface. Generic hooks (function useList<T>(...): [T[], (item: T) => void]) let one implementation serve many payload types, which is the typed replacement for wrapper components that once existed only to inject props, while the classic wrapper form stays justified when the reuse is structural rather than behavioural.
pitfalls: Types cannot enforce the rules of hooks: a conditionally called hook still type-checks while displacing state, so the lint rules remain mandatory.
State types inferred from the initial value can widen or collapse to a union at call sites; annotate explicitly (useState<Status>) when the initial value does not pin the type.
A context created as createContext<T | null>(null) forces every consumer to guard; provide a throwing accessor hook or a non-null provider contract instead of casting the result.

variants.name: Typed Vue composables (Composition API in TypeScript)
variants.idiom_name: typed Composition API composables returning Ref<T>/ComputedRef<T>
variants.implementation_notes: Vue composables are normally written in TypeScript, where ref<T>() and computed<T>() carry the state types and the composable's return type documents the reactive surface; the unit is again a plain function calling Composition API primitives, so the same generics discipline applies as for React hooks. Nesting and per-component-instance state semantics are unchanged, and shared state still belongs to a store rather than to a composable.
pitfalls: Ref<T> unwrapping in templates hides .value, so a typed API that returns a ref behaves differently depending on where it is consumed; keep the return contract consistent.
Destructuring a reactive object returned by a composable loses reactivity unless toRefs() is used, and the type system will not warn you.
